questions.question: What is LMCache's primary role in the vLLM production stack?
options: A load balancer that routes requests based on cache affinity
A KV offloading layer that extracts KV cache from GPU HBM to CPU DRAM or disk and reuses it across queries and engines
A model weight compression tool that reduces HBM usage by 50%
An observability collector that aggregates Prometheus metrics from vLLM workers
questions.explanation: LMCache is the KV offloading layer: it extracts KV cache from GPU HBM to CPU DRAM (and then optionally disk/Ceph) and reuses those KV blocks across queries and across multiple vLLM engine instances. This is distinct from model weight compression.

questions.question: The vLLM 0.11.0 KV Offloading Connector (January 2026) made offloading asynchronous. Why does this matter?
options: It allows LMCache to run on a separate Kubernetes node without additional configuration
Offload latency is no longer user-visible — the write to CPU DRAM happens while the GPU continues serving other requests
It enables LMCache to synchronously verify data integrity after each write
Asynchronous offloading doubles the effective HBM bandwidth
questions.explanation: With the asynchronous Connector API (v0.9.0+), KV blocks are offloaded to CPU DRAM in the background while the GPU continues processing. The offload latency is decoupled from the user-facing request latency.

questions.question: When is LMCache most valuable, even without shared prefix reuse across requests?
options: When model weights exceed available HBM capacity
When a GPU runs out of KV slots and preempted requests can be restored from CPU DRAM instead of recomputing prefill
When multiple LoRA adapters are loaded simultaneously
When requests have identical system prompts across all users
questions.explanation: LMCache provides value even without shared prefixes: when the GPU exhausts KV slots and must preempt requests, it can restore them from CPU DRAM instead of re-running expensive prefill. The restore cost is much lower than recomputation.

questions.question: At what KV cache footprint does LMCache start adding overhead without benefit?
options: When KV cache exceeds 50% of HBM capacity
When KV footprint is low (short prompts, low concurrency) and fits comfortably in HBM
When the system prompt is longer than 4,096 tokens
When more than 8 engine replicas share the LMCache layer
questions.explanation: The lesson's benchmark behavior: at low KV footprint (short prompts, low concurrency), all configurations match baseline and LMCache adds ~3-5% overhead with no benefit. LMCache becomes decisive when KV pressure is high or cross-engine sharing is needed.

questions.question: Which deployment scenario is explicitly called out as NOT benefiting from LMCache?
options: Multi-tenant serving with shared system prompts across tenants
RAG where document chunks repeat across queries
Single-tenant single-prompt workload with no repeated content
LoRA fine-tuned variants on the same base model
questions.explanation: Single-tenant single-prompt workloads have no KV reuse to capture — every request is unique. LMCache adds 3-5% overhead without benefit in this case. The lesson recommends against enabling it for workloads with no reuse pattern.

questions.question: The vLLM production-stack has four main layers. Which is the correct list?
options: Model registry, serving engine, observability, billing
Router, engines, KV cache offload, observability
Load balancer, GPU pool, storage, monitoring
Gateway, inference server, database, CDN
questions.explanation: The vLLM production-stack layers: router (cache-aware, consumes KV events), engines (vLLM workers per GPU or TP/PP group), KV cache offload (LMCache or native connector), and observability (Prometheus/Grafana/OTel).
